summary: Jonathan Liew reports on Manchester United's stirring win over Chelsea at Old Trafford after defeat at Newcastle, arguing it came amid dressing-room turmoil stories around Erik ten Hag. He highlights United's all-out attacking approach (28 shots, 4.07 xG) and Scott McTominay's role as a roaming, goal-scoring midfielder with two goals. The piece frames Ten Hag's approach as a high-risk gamble that leaves gaps at the back but may become sustainable once key players return.
one_line: Manchester United beat Chelsea with an all-out attacking gamble from Erik ten Hag, driven by Scott McTominay's two goals and free-roaming midfield role.
key_facts: Manchester United beat Chelsea at Old Trafford after losing at Newcastle, leaving them three points behind Manchester City.
United had 28 shots and an xG tally of 4.07 against Chelsea, yet hung on at the end.
Scott McTominay scored his fifth and sixth goals of the season; previously he had never scored more than seven in a season.
McTominay has a licence to create overloads, appearing in the penalty area, channels and on the wing, and is compared to Paul Pogba's former role.
Both teams hollowed out their midfields: United to throw bodies forward, Chelsea to leave men up for the breakaway.
Chelsea's goal came from two vertical passes through the centre via Mykhailo Mudryk to Cole Palmer.
Nicolas Jackson is described as looking like a man playing football in a hall of mirrors for his finishing against United's open defence.
Diogo Dalot was flying forward from right-back even as the minutes ticked down.
Ten Hag's gamble depends on Lisandro Martínez and Raphaël Varane returning, the defensive line moving up 10 yards, and Rasmus Højlund and Mason Mount finding form.
United's next match is against Bournemouth on Saturday, where Dominic Solanke is mentioned as a threat.
Liew says the win may only buy Ten Hag a few days' grace amid stories of dressing-room discontent.
Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire are credited with leadership qualities, but tactically McTominay is running the show.
